title: R’ Yonatan ben Chagai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Kohelet Rabbah 9:12, R’ Azaryah and R’ Yonatan ben Chagai report in R’ Yitzchak bar Marion’s name in R’ Chanina’s name: “You may find a person who sins on earth and does not sin in heaven,” etc.
In Bereshit Rabbah 42:7 they both speak in R’ Yitzchak’s name; Hyman suggests it is possible that the words “bar Marion” are missing.
In his citation of Midrash Shmuel 22:5, Hyman has the same two sages report in R’ Yitzchak bar Marion’s name: “The strictness of fathers is better than the meekness of sons.”

In the passage he cites as Tanchuma, Reeh 16, Hyman has R’ Azaryah, R’ Yonatan ben Chagai, and R’ Yitzchak bar Marion report in the name of R’ Yose son of R’ Chanina [supplied ריבר״ח, expanded from Hyman’s parallel notice]: “One who eats his produce while it is untithed is as one who eats carrion and torn animals.”

notes.text: The final abbreviated transmitter ריבר״ח remains unidentified. Hyman’s proposal to restore bar Marion in Bereshit Rabbah is only a conjecture.

The whole local frozen packet017 spells the SAME TanchumaReeh16 chain as Yose son of Chanina. This supports the internal name expansion of ריבר״ח; it does not supply full Rabbi titles, an independently inspected Tanchuma witness, or an admitted genealogy. The parallel itself has only R-prime titles. Kohelet9:12/Bereshit42:7/Shmuel22:5 are chapter-section readings, not chapter ranges. Hyman’s POSSIBLE missing bar Marion stays conjectural; both joined reporters and the final THREE joined reporters remain. The warning about untithed produce, carrion AND torn animals keeps all terms; classification holds remain pending a separate gate.

In Kohelet Rabbah 9:12 the consulted Hebrew calls him Yonatan be-Rabbi Chagai. Bereshit Rabbah 42:7 gives Yitzchak without bar Marion, which Hyman conjectures may be missing. The consulted Krakow Midrash Shmuel 22:5 names Zecharyah alongside Yonatan bar Chagai, where Hyman carries forward Azaryah. Buber’s Tanchuma Reeh 16 has the three joint transmitters and gives Yose בר״ח. The corresponding Hebrew passage in the Torat Emet text is at Reeh 17 and gives Yonatan and Yose bar Chananyah. The English translation accompanying that text gives Johanan. Hyman’s parallel notice on Yitzchak bar Marion instead spells out Yose son of Chanina. These readings leave the variation in the final name visible.
